en: In what has been said about the concept of this science and where its justification lies, it is implicit that the general division can here be only provisional, and can be indicated only to the extent that the author already knows the science, and is therefore able to state here in advance, historically, to what main distinctions the concept will determine itself in its development.
zh: 在关于这门科学的概念及其正当性何在所说的那些话里，已经包含着这样一点：这里的一般划分只能是暂定的；它只能被指明到这样的程度——即作者已经知道这门科学，因而能够在事先就从历史的角度指出：这个概念将在其发展中被规定为哪些主要区别。

en: Nevertheless it can be attempted to make intelligible in advance and in general what is required for dividing, even though here too a procedure of the method has to be employed which only within the science receives its full explication and justification.
— First of all, then, it is to be recalled that here it is presupposed that the division must be connected with the concept, or rather that it must lie in the concept itself.

The concept is not indeterminate but determinate in itself; the division, however, expresses this its determinateness in developed form; it is the judgement of the concept, not a judgement about any object taken up externally, but the judging, i.e. the determining, of the concept in itself.

Right-angledness, acute-angledness, etc., as well as equilaterality, etc. — the determinations according to which triangles are divided — do not lie in the determinateness of the triangle itself, that is, not in what is commonly called the concept of the triangle; no more than they lie in what holds for the concept of the animal in general or of the mammal, the bird, etc., namely in the determinations according to which the former is divided into mammals, birds, etc., and these classes into further genera.
Such determinations are taken up from elsewhere, from empirical intuition; they come in from outside to that so-called concept.
In the philosophical treatment of division, the concept itself must show itself as containing their origin in it.
zh: 不过人们可以尝试，事先从一般方面把作划分所必需的东西讲清楚；尽管在这里也必须动用方法的一个程序，而这个程序只有在科学内部才得到充分的说明与正当化。
——首先应当提醒的是：这里所预设的是，划分必须与概念相联系，或者更确切地说，必须就存在于概念本身之中。
概念并不是不确定的，而是自在地确定的；但划分是以展开的方式表达出它的这一规定性；划分是概念的判断，不是对任何从外面取来的对象的判断，而是判断活动本身，即在概念自身上对概念加以规定。
直角性、锐角性等等，以及等边性等等——三角形据以被划分的那些规定——并不在三角形自身的规定性之中，也就是不在通常被称作三角形的概念之中；它们同样也不在那些适用于动物的一般概念、或哺乳动物、鸟等等的概念的规定之中，即不在那个把前者划分为哺乳动物、鸟类等等、并把这些类别再划分为更进一步的种属的规定之中。
这样的规定是从别处、从经验直观中采取的；它们是从外面加到那个所谓的概念上的。
在对划分作哲学处理时，概念本身必须显示为在自身中包含着划分的起源。

en: The concept of logic itself, however, has been given in the Introduction as the result of a science lying beyond, and hence has been stated here too as a presupposition.

Logic was accordingly determined as the science of pure thinking, which has pure knowledge for its principle, a unity which is not abstract but thereby concrete and living, in that within it the opposition of consciousness between a subject existing for itself and a second such existing, an objective one, is known to have been overcome, and being is known as the pure concept in itself, and the pure concept as the true being.
These are therefore the two moments which are contained in the logical.

But they are now known to be inseparable, not, as in consciousness, each of them also as existing for itself; by this alone, namely by their being known at the same time as distinguished (though not as existing for themselves), is their unity not abstract, dead, unmoving, but concrete.
zh: 然而，逻辑学自身的概念在导言中已被指明为那种处在彼岸的科学的成果，因而在这里也同样被指明为一个预设。
逻辑学据此被规定为纯粹思维的科学，它以纯粹知识为原则；而这纯粹知识不是抽象的，而是这样一个具体而有生气的统一：在其中，意识关于一个自为存在的主观者与第二个同样自为存在者、亦即一个客体的对立被知为已经克服，存在被知为自在纯粹的纯粹概念，而纯粹概念被知为真正的存在。
因此，这就是包含在逻辑中的两个环节。
但如今它们被知为不可分，而不像在意识中那样每一个还被知为自为存在；唯其如此，即唯其同时被知为有差别的（但不是自为存在的），它们的统一才是具体的，而不是抽象的、死寂的、呆板的。

en: This unity accordingly makes the logical principle into an element at the same time, so that the development of that difference which is immediately present in it takes place only within this element.

For since the division, as has been said, is the judgement of the concept, the positing of the determination already immanent in it and hence of its difference, this positing must not be taken as a dissolution back of that concrete unity into its determinations, as they are supposed to be valid as existing for themselves; that would here be an empty going back to the previous standpoint, the opposition of consciousness; this has rather disappeared; that unity remains the element, and from it that distinguishing of the division and of development in general no longer issues.

Thus the determinations which earlier (on the way to truth) existed for themselves, such as the subjective and the objective, or also thinking and being, or concept and reality, however they may have been determined in any respect, are now reduced to forms in their truth, i.e. in their unity.
In their difference, therefore, they themselves remain in themselves the whole concept, and this concept is posited in the division only under its own determinations.
zh: 因此，这一统一使逻辑的原则同时成为元素；因而那种差别——它当下就在这原则之内——的发展只在这个元素之内进行。
因为划分如前所述乃是概念的判断，是把那个已经内含于概念之中的规定、因而也就是它的差别设定起来，所以这一设定不得被理解为把那个具体的统一重新消解为它的各项规定（仿佛这些规定是作为自为存在的东西而成立的）；那在这里将会是对先前立场、亦即意识之对立的空洞倒退；而这一对立毋宁已经消失；那个统一仍然是元素，而划分的、乃至发展本身的那种区别也不再从它里面出来。
这样一来，那些先前（在通往真理的道路上）自为存在的规定——如主观者与客体者，或思维与存在，或概念与实在性，不论它们曾在何种角度下被规定——如今都在它们的真理中、即在它们的统一中，被降低为形式。
因此在它们的差别中，它们自在地本身仍是整个概念；而这个概念在划分中只是被设定在它自己的各项规定之下。

en: Thus it is the whole concept which is to be regarded now as the concept of being, now as concept as such; there it is only the concept in itself, the concept of reality or of being; here it is the concept as such, the concept existing for itself (as it is, to name concrete forms, in the thinking human being, but also already in the feeling animal and in the organic individual in general, admittedly not as a conscious and still less as a known concept); the concept in itself, however, it is only in inorganic nature.

— Logic would accordingly first have to be divided into the logic of the concept as being and of the concept as concept, or — if we use the otherwise usual expressions, which are indeed the most indeterminate and therefore the most ambiguous — into objective and subjective logic.
zh: 因此是那个整个概念：它有时应当被看作存在的概念，有时应当被看作概念本身；在那里（作为存在的概念中）它还只是自在的概念，即实在性或存在的概念；在这里（作为概念本身中）它是自为存在的概念——举出具体的形态来说：它固然在思维着的人那里、但也早已在感受着的动物以及一般有机的个体那里，还并不是作为被意识的、更不是作为被知识的概念；自在的概念则仅仅在无机自然中。
——因此，逻辑学首先应当划分为「作为存在的概念」的逻辑学与「作为概念的概念」的逻辑学；或者——如果我们沿用那些通常的、虽然最不确定因而也最多歧义的表达——划分为客观逻辑学与主观逻辑学。

en: Now since what underlies this is the element of the unity of the concept in itself, and with it the inseparability of its determinations, these must further, insofar as they are distinguished and the concept is posited in their difference, at least stand in relation to one another.

There emerges from this a sphere of mediation, the concept as a system of reflection-determinations, i.e. of being which passes over into the being-in-itself of the concept, which in this way is not yet posited as such for itself, but is at the same time afflicted with immediate being as something also external to it.
This is the doctrine of essence, which stands in the midst between the doctrine of being and the doctrine of the concept.

— In the general division of this logical work it has still been placed under the objective logic, although essence is already the inner, while the character of the subject is expressly reserved to the concept.
zh: 然而，由于所依据的是概念在自身中的统一这一元素，因而也是它的各项规定的不可分性，所以这些规定进一步地——就它们被区别开、概念被设定在它们的差别中而言——至少还必须彼此处于关系之中。
由此产生出一个中介的领域：概念作为反思规定的体系，即作为那种过渡到概念的自身内存在的存在；这种存在以这种方式还没有作为这样的东西被设定为自为存在，而是同时还带有直接的存在、也就是一种对概念来说同样是外在的东西。
这就是关于本质的学说，它处在关于存在的学说与关于概念的学说之间。
——在这部逻辑著作的一般划分中，本质学说还被列在客观逻辑学之下，尽管本质已经即是内部的东西，而主体的性质则被明确地保留给概念。

en: Kant5 has in recent times set up alongside what is commonly called logic yet another logic, namely a transcendental logic.
What is here called objective logic would in part correspond to what for him is transcendental logic.

He distinguishes it from what he calls general logic in such a way that it α considers the concepts which relate to objects a priori, and so does not abstract from all the content of objective cognition, or that it contains the rules of the pure thinking of an object, and β at the same time goes into the origin of our cognition insofar as this cannot be ascribed to the objects.
— It is this second aspect exclusively to which Kant’s philosophical interest is directed.
His main thought is to vindicate the categories to self-consciousness, as the subjective I.

By virtue of this determination the standpoint remains within consciousness and its opposition, and besides the empirical element of feeling and intuition something that is not posited and determined by thinking self-consciousness — a thing-in-itself, something foreign and external to thought — remains over and above; although it is easy to see that an abstraction such as the thing-in-itself is itself only a product of thinking, and of abstracting thinking in particular.

— If other Kantians have expressed the determining of the object through the I in such a way that the objectification of the I is to be regarded as an original and necessary act of consciousness, so that in this original act the representation of the I itself is not yet present — for which a consciousness of that consciousness, or itself an objectification of that consciousness, is required first —, then this act of objectification, freed from the opposition of consciousness, is closer to that which can be taken as thinking as such in general.6 This act, however, should no longer be called consciousness; consciousness includes within itself the opposition of the I and its object, which is not present in that original act.

The designation “consciousness” casts still more the appearance of subjectivity over the same thing than the expression “thinking”, which is however here to be taken in the absolute sense as infinite thinking, not affected by the finitude of consciousness, in short as thinking as such.
zh: 康德5在近代把另一种逻辑、即先验逻辑学，与通常被称作逻辑学的东西相对列出来。
这里被称作客观逻辑学的东西，有一部分会相当于他所谓的先验逻辑学。
他把先验逻辑学与他所谓的普遍逻辑学区分开来，其区分的方式是：先验逻辑学 α 考察那些先天（a priori）地关涉对象的概念，因而并不撇开客观认识的一切内容；或者说，它包含对某一对象的纯粹思维规则，并且 β 同时追究我们认识的起源，只要这起源不能被归给对象本身。
——康德的哲学兴趣所专一指向的，正是这第二个方面。
他的主要想法是：把范畴归给自我意识、即归给主观的我。
凭借这一规定，这一立场便始终停留在意识及其对立之内；除了感受与直观中的经验之东西以外，还残留着某种并非由思维的自我意识所设定和规定的东西——一个自在之物，一个对于思维而言是外在的、外来的东西；尽管很容易看出：像自在之物这样的抽象，本身也只是思维的、而且仅仅只是抽象的思维的一个产物。

——如果别的康德主义者这样表述「由我来规定对象」：自我的对象化应当被看作意识的一个原始而必然的行为，以至于在这个原始行为中还没有自我的表象——因为自我的表象首先需要一种对那个意识的意识，或者干脆说需要那个意识的对象化——那么这个从意识的对立中解放出来的对象化的行为，就更接近于那一般地可以被当作思维本身的东西。6 不过这一行为就不该再被称作意识；意识本身包含着「我」与其对象之间的对立，而这一对立在那个原始行为中是不存在的。
称作「意识」比称作「思维」更给同一个东西蒙上主观性的假象；不过这里的「思维」是要在绝对意义上来取的，即取那种无限的、不为意识的有限性所累的思维，简言之，取思维本身。

en: Now since the interest of Kantian philosophy was directed to what is called the transcendental of the determinations of thought, the treatment of them themselves has turned out empty; what they are in themselves, apart from the abstract, the same for all, relation to the I, their determinateness as against one another and their relation to one another, has not been made an object of consideration; the knowledge of their nature has therefore in the least been advanced by this philosophy.
The only interesting thing which has a bearing on this occurs in the criticism of the ideas.

But for the actual progress of philosophy it was necessary that the interest of thinking should be drawn to the consideration of the formal side, of the I, of consciousness as such, i.e. of the abstract relation of a subjective knowledge to an object, and that the knowledge of the infinite form, i.e. of the concept, should in this way have been initiated.
However, in order to reach this knowledge, that finite determinateness in which the form is as I, as consciousness, still had to be stripped off.

The form, thought out thus into its purity, then contains within itself the determination of itself, i.e. the giving to itself of content, and that content in its necessity, — as a system of the determinations of thought.
zh: 现在，既然康德哲学的兴趣是朝向思维规定的所谓先验方面，那么对这些规定本身的论述就归于空疏；它们自在地是什么——撇开那种对「我」的、对一切人都一样的抽象关系，撇开它们彼此相对的规定性以及它们彼此间的关系——并没有被当作考察的对象；因此，对它们本性的认识，通过这门哲学丝毫也没有得到推进。
唯一与这一点相关联的东西，出现在对观念的批判之中。
但对哲学的现实推进来说却是必需的：思维的兴趣应当被引向对形式方面、对我、对作为这样的意识，亦即对主观的知识与一个客体之间的抽象关系的考察；而对无限的形式、亦即对概念的认识，正是以此方式被开启的。
然而，为了达到这一认识，那有限的规定性——形式作为我、作为意识所处的那种有限的规定性——还必须被剥除。
这样被思入其纯粹性的形式，于是就在自身中包含着对自身的规定，即包含着给予自身以内容——而且是给予那处于其必然性之中的内容——也就是作为思维规定的体系。

en: The objective logic thus rather takes the place of the former metaphysics, which was the scientific edifice over the world, which was to be erected only by thought.

— If we take into account the final shape of the development of this science, then it is, first, immediately, ontology which the objective logic replaces, — the part of that metaphysics which should have investigated the nature of the ens in general; the ens comprehends both being and essence in itself, for which distinction our language has fortunately preserved a different expression.

— But in the second place the objective logic also comprehends the rest of metaphysics in itself, insofar as that metaphysics sought to grasp with the pure forms of thought the particular substrates, taken in the first instance from representation — the soul, the world, God — and the determinations of thought constituted the essential feature of its mode of consideration.
But logic considers these forms free of those substrates, the subjects of representation, and their nature and worth in and for themselves.

That metaphysics neglected this and therefore drew upon itself the just reproach of having used them without criticism, without the preliminary investigation of whether and how they are capable of being determinations of the thing-in-itself — in Kant’s phrase — or rather of the rational.

— The objective logic is therefore the true criticism of them — a criticism which does not consider them according to the abstract form of the a priori against the a posteriori, but considers them themselves in their particular content.
zh: 因此，客观逻辑学毋宁是取代了从前的形而上学；后者是那座架于世界之上的科学建筑，而这座建筑只应当靠思想来建成。
——如果我们顾及这门科学发展的最后形态，那么首先，客观逻辑学直接取代的就是本体论——即形而上学中本应研究存在物本身之本性的那一部分；存在物在自身中既包含存在也包含本质，而我们的语言幸运地为这一差别保存了不同的表达。
——其次，客观逻辑学在其自身中同样包含着形而上学的其余部分：就后者曾试图用纯粹的思维形式去把握那些特殊的、首先从表象中取得的基底——灵魂、世界、上帝——并且思维的诸规定构成其考察方式的本质而言。
但逻辑学是撇开那些基底、撇开表象的主体来考察这些形式的，并考察它们自在自为的本性与价值。
那门形而上学没有做这一点，因而招来了它应得的指责：它不经批判地使用了这些形式，没有事先考察这些形式是否、以及如何能够是自在之物——按康德的说法——或者更确切地说是理性之物的规定。
——因此，客观逻辑学就是对这些形式真正的批判——一种不是按照先验性的抽象形式把它们与后天的东西相对立，而是就它们各自的特殊内容来考察它们的批判。

en: The subjective logic is the logic of the concept, — of the essence which has cancelled its relation to a being or to its appearance, and in its determination is no longer something external, but the free, self-subsistent, self-determining subjective or rather the subject itself.

— Since the subjective carries with it the confusion of the contingent and the arbitrary, and in general of determinations which belong to the form of consciousness, no particular weight is to be laid here on the distinction between the subjective and the objective, which will be developed more closely later on within the logic itself.
zh: 主观逻辑学是概念的逻辑学——是那个本质的逻辑学：它已扬弃了自己与一个存在或与自己的假象的关系，在它的规定中它不再是一个外在的东西，而是自由的、独立自主的、在自身中规定自己的主观者，或者更确切地说，就是主体本身。
——由于主观者随身带着对偶然与任性的、以及总的说来对那些属于意识形式的规定的误解，所以这里不必特别看重主观与客观之间的差别；这一差别随后将在逻辑学内部得到更充分的展开。

en: Logic therefore does indeed divide in general into objective and subjective logic; more precisely, however, it has the three parts:
zh: 因此，逻辑学总的说来虽分为客观逻辑学与主观逻辑学；但更确切地说，它有如下三个部分：

en: I. The logic of being,
zh: I. 存在的逻辑学，

en: II. the logic of essence and
zh: II. 本质的逻辑学，以及

en: III. the logic of the concept.
zh: III. 概念的逻辑学。

15.en: First Book. The Doctrine of Being
15.zh: 第一卷　存在的学说

16.en: With What Must the Beginning of Science Be Made?
16.zh: 科学必须以什么为开端？

en: It is only in more recent times that the consciousness has arisen that there is a difficulty in finding a beginning in philosophy, and the ground of this difficulty as well as the possibility of resolving it has been treated in many ways.

The beginning of philosophy must be either something mediated or something immediate, and it is easy to show that it can be neither the one nor the other; thus each or either way of beginning is refuted.
zh: 只是到了近代，人们才意识到：在哲学中找到一个开端乃是一件有困难的事；而这一困难的根据以及解决它的可能性，则已得到多种多样的讨论。
哲学的开端必须是一个被中介的东西或一个直接的东西；而很容易表明，它既不能是前者也不能是后者；于是，这一种或那一种开端方式都遭到了反驳。

en: The principle of a philosophy does indeed also express a beginning, but not so much a subjective as an objective one, the beginning of all things.
The principle is a determinate content in some way: the water, the One, nous, the Idea,

— substance, monad, etc.; or if it relates to the nature of cognition and is thereby to be rather a criterion than an objective determination — thinking, intuition, sensation, the I, subjectivity itself —, then here too it is the determination of content on which the interest rests.

The beginning as such, on the contrary, remains, as something subjective in the sense of an accidental manner of introducing the exposition, unnoticed and indifferent; and thus the need of the question as to what to begin with is insignificant in comparison with the need of the principle, in which alone the interest of the matter seems to lie, the interest as to what the true is, what the absolute ground of everything is.
zh: 一个哲学的原则固然也表达着一个开端，但它所表达的不是主观的开端，而是客观的开端，即一切事物的开端。
原则是某种以某种方式被规定的内容：水、一、nous、观念、
——实体、单子等等；或者，如果它涉及认识的本性，并因而更多地只是一个判准而不是一种客观规定——思维、直观、感受、我、主观性本身——那么在这里，兴趣所指向的同样也是那种内容的规定。
而作为这样的开端则相反，它仍然是主观的，就其意义而言，它只是为引出讲述而采取的一种偶然方式，因而是无足轻重、漠然无所谓的；这样一来，「以什么开始」这一问题的需要，相对于原则的需要也就无关紧要了，因为唯独在原则中才似乎有着事情本身的兴趣：即那真的者是什么、一切之绝对根据是什么的兴趣。

en: But the modern embarrassment about the beginning arises from a further need which those do not yet know for whom it is dogmatically a matter of proving the principle or sceptically a matter of finding a subjective criterion against dogmatic philosophizing, and which those entirely deny who want to begin like something out of a pistol, out of their inner revelation, out of faith, intellectual intuition, etc., and to be lifted above method and logic.

If the earlier abstract thinking is at first interested only in the principle as content, but in the course of its formation is driven to pay attention to the other side, to the behaviour of cognition, then the subjective act too is comprehended as an essential moment of the objective truth, and the need presents itself that method be united with content, form with principle.
Thus the principle is also to be the beginning, and what is the prius for thinking is also to be the first in the course of thinking.
zh: 然而近代对开端的窘迫，出自一种进一步的需要：那些独断地关乎原则的证明、或怀疑地关乎寻找一个反对独断式哲学的准则的人，还不认识这种需要；而那些像从枪膛里射出来一样，从自己内心的启示、从信仰、从智性直观等等开始，并想要凌驾于方法与逻辑学之上的人，则完全否认这种需要。
如果早先的抽象思维起初只对作为内容的原则感兴趣，但在其形成的进程中却被驱使去关注另一面、关注认识的行为，那么主观的行为也就被把握为客观真理的一个本质环节，而那种需要也就随之而来：方法须与内容相结合，形式须与原则相结合。
这样，原则就应当同时是开端；而那对思维而言是先于一切的东西，也应当是思维进程中的第一者。

en: Here we only have to consider how the logical beginning appears; the two aspects according to which it can be taken have already been named, either as a result in a mediated way or as a proper beginning in an immediate way.

The question which appears so important in the education of the time, whether the knowledge of truth is an immediate, simply beginning knowledge, a faith, or on the other hand a mediated knowledge, is not to be discussed at this point.
Insofar as such a consideration can be undertaken provisionally, this has been done elsewhere (in my Encyclopedia of the Philosophical Sciences, 3.
edition, in the “Preliminary Concept”, § 61 ff.)

From this we may adduce only so much: that there is nothing, nothing in heaven or in nature or in spirit or wherever it may be, which does not contain the immediacy as much as the mediation, so that these two determinations show themselves as undivided and inseparable, and that opposition as something nil.

But with regard to the scientific discussion, it is every logical proposition in which the determinations of immediacy and mediation, and so the discussion of their opposition and of their truth, occur.

Insofar as this opposition, in relation to thinking, knowledge, cognition, takes on the more concrete shape of immediate or mediated knowledge, the nature of cognition in general is considered both within the science of logic, and the same falls, in its further concrete form, into the science of spirit and its phenomenology.

To want to get at cognition cleanly already before science means to demand that it should be discussed outside of science; outside of science this can at least not be achieved in a scientific way, which alone is what is at issue here.
zh: 这里只需考察逻辑的开端如何呈现出来；它可以从两个方面来取，这一点已经说过了：或者是以被中介的方式作为结果，或者是以直接的方式作为真正的开端。
在时代的教养中显得如此重要的那个问题——真理的知识究竟是一种直接的、纯粹开端的知识、一种信仰，还是一种被中介的知识——在此处是不必讨论的。
就这种考察可以暂作而言，这一点已在别处做过（见我的《哲学科学全书》，第 3.
版，「前概念」，§ 61 及以下）
这里由此只须指出这一点：没有任何东西——天上、自然中、精神中或无论何处的任何东西——不是同样地既包含直接性又包含中介，以至于这两个规定显示为未分且不可分，而那个对立显示为无。
但就科学的论述而言，它就是每一个这样的逻辑命题：在其中出现直接性与中介的规定，因而出现对它们的对立及其真理的论述。
就这一对立在涉及思维、知识、认识时取得直接的知识或被中介的知识这一更具体的形态而言，认识的本性一方面在逻辑学这门科学之内受到考察，另一方面在它更具体的形态中则落入精神科学及其现象学之中。
但在科学之前就想要把认识彻底弄清楚，就等于要求认识应当在科学之外得到论述；而在科学之外，这件事至少不能以科学的方式——而这里所涉及的恰恰只是这种方式——来完成。

en: Logically the beginning is made in the element of thinking existing freely for itself, in pure knowledge.
It is thereby mediated, in that pure knowledge is the last, absolute truth of consciousness.

It has been noted in the Introduction that the phenomenology of spirit is the science of consciousness, the presentation of the fact that consciousness has the concept of science, i.e. pure knowledge, as its result.

The logic has therefore as its presupposition the science of appearing spirit, which contains and exhibits the necessity, and with it the proof of the truth, of the standpoint of pure knowledge, as well as its mediation in general.
In this science of appearing spirit the start is made from the empirical, sensuous consciousness, and this is the proper immediate knowledge; there what lies in this immediate knowledge is discussed.

Another consciousness, such as faith in divine truths, inner experience, knowledge through inner revelation, etc., shows itself, on slight consideration, to be very improperly listed as immediate knowledge.

In that treatise the immediate consciousness is also the first and immediate in science, and hence the presupposition; but in logic it is what has proved itself in that consideration to be the result that is the presupposition, — the idea as pure knowledge.
Logic is the pure science, i.e. pure knowledge in the whole range of its development.

This idea, however, has determined itself in that result to be the certainty which has become truth, the certainty which on the one side no longer stands over against the object but has made it internal, has known it as itself, — and which on the other side has given up the knowledge of itself as of one which stands over against the objective and is only its destruction, has externalised this subjectivity and is unity with its externalisation.
zh: 在逻辑上，开端是在自由地自为存在的思维这一元素中、在纯粹知识之中做出的。
它由此是被中介的，因为纯粹知识是意识的最后、绝对真理。
导言中已经指出：《精神现象学》是关于意识的科学，是对意识以科学的概念、亦即以纯粹知识为结果这一事实的呈现。
因此，逻辑学以显现的精神这门科学为预设；这门科学包含并展示出纯粹知识这一立场的必然性，从而也展示出这一立场的真理的证明，以及它总体的中介。
在显现的精神这门科学中，人们是从经验的、感性的意识出发的，而这个意识才是真正的直接知识；在那里人们所论述的，正是这种直接知识中所含的东西。
另一些意识——例如对神圣真理的信仰、内在的经验、通过内在启示而来的知识等等——稍加思索便可看出，把它们列在直接知识之下是极不恰当的。
在那部论著中，直接的意识同时也是科学中最初和最直接的东西，因而就是预设；但在逻辑学中，预设的却是从那种考察中已被证明为结果的东西——作为纯粹知识的观念。
逻辑学是纯粹的科学，即纯粹知识在其全部发展范围中的样子。
然而这一观念在那个结果中把自己规定为那已成为真理的确定性：这确定性在一方面不再与对象相对立，而是已经把对象变成内在的、把对象认作自己；另一方面，它又放弃了那种关于自身的知识——即不再把自己认作是那种与对象之物相对立、并且只是对象之毁灭者；它已经把这种主观性外化了，并且就是与它自己的外化相统一。

en: That the beginning of the science of pure knowledge should remain immanent from this determination of pure knowledge is nothing more than to consider it, or rather to take up simply what is present, putting aside all reflections and all opinions one might otherwise have.
zh: 至于从纯粹知识的这一规定出发，纯粹知识这门科学的开端仍保持在内在（而不越出）——这无须别的，只需要考察它，或者更确切地说，把人们通常持有的种种反思、种种意见撇在一边，只把现有的东西接纳下来。

en: Pure knowledge, having come together into this unity, has cancelled all relation to an other and to mediation; it is the undifferentiated; this undifferentiated therefore itself ceases to be knowledge; there is only simple immediacy present.
zh: 纯粹知识既已汇合为这一统一，就扬弃了它与它者的一切关系以及与中介的一切关系；它就是那无差别者；而这无差别者因此本身就不再是知识；所剩下的只有单纯直接性。

en: Simple immediacy is itself an expression of reflection and refers to the difference from the mediated.
In its true expression, therefore, this simple immediacy is pure being.

As pure knowledge is to mean nothing other than knowledge as such, quite abstract, so too pure being is to mean nothing other than being in general: being, and nothing else, without all further determination and fulfilment.
zh: 单纯直接性本身是一个反思的表达，并且指向与被中介者的差别。
因此，在它真正的表达中，这单纯直接性就是纯粹的存在。
正如纯粹知识除了作为这样的知识、全然抽象的知识之外不意味着别的什么，纯粹的存在同样除了作为一般的存在之外也不意味着别的什么：只是存在，此外别无任何，没有一切进一步的规定与充实。

en: Here being is the beginning-and-end, presented as having arisen through mediation, and indeed through a mediation which is at the same time the sublation of itself; with the presupposition of pure knowledge as the result of finite knowledge, of consciousness.

But if no presupposition is to be made and the beginning itself is to be taken immediately, then it is determined only by the fact that it is to be the beginning of logic, of thinking existing for itself.
Only the resolve — which one may also take for an arbitrariness — namely to consider thinking as such, is present.

Thus the beginning must be an absolute or, what is equivalent here, an abstract beginning; it may in that way presuppose nothing, must be mediated through nothing nor have any ground; it is rather to be itself the ground of the whole science.
It must therefore be simply an immediate, or rather it must be only the immediate itself.

As it cannot have a determination with respect to something other, so it also cannot have one in itself, cannot contain any content, for such a thing would be a distinguishing of the diverse and a relation of the diverse to one another, and hence a mediation.
The beginning is therefore pure being.
zh: 在这里，存在是那开端即终结者，是作为通过中介——而且是通过同时扬弃其自身的中介——而产生出来的东西被呈现出来的；并以纯粹知识为预设，而纯粹知识是有限的知识、即意识的成果。
但如果不应作任何预设、而应当直接把握开端本身，那么它就仅仅由这样一点来规定：它应当是逻辑学的开端，是自为存在的思维的开端。
所存在的不过是这样一个决意——人们也可以把它看作一种任性——即要考察思维本身。
所以开端必须是绝对的、或者——在这里二者是同义的——抽象的开端；它如此则不得预设任何东西，必须不由任何东西中介而来，也不具有任何根据；毋宁说，它本身应当是整门科学的根据。
所以它干脆必须是一个直接者，或者更确切地说，必须只是那直接者本身。
既然它不可能对他物具有任何规定，它也不可能自身内具有规定，不可能包含任何内容；因为这样的东西将是对相异者彼此的区别以及相异者相互之间的关系，因而就是一种中介。
所以开端就是纯粹的存在。

en: After this simple exposition of what initially belongs only to this simplest of all itself, the logical beginning, the following further reflections can still be brought forward; but they cannot serve both to elucidate and to confirm that exposition, which is finished in itself, as they are rather called forth only by representations and reflections which can come in our way in advance, yet which, like all the other preceding prejudices, must find their dispatch in the science itself, and so it would really be advisable to point patience to this.
zh: 在这样简要地陈述了起初仅仅属于这最简单者自身、即逻辑开端的东西之后，还可以补充如下进一步的反思；不过这些反思不能既用来阐释又用来确认那已经自身完结的陈述，它们毋宁只是由一些可能预先挡在我们路上的表象与反思所引起的；而它们——像所有其他先行的偏见一样——必须在科学自身之中得到了结，因此实际上人们大可在此提醒人们耐心等待。

en: The insight that the absolute truth must be a result, and conversely that a result presupposes a first truth which, because it is the first, is objectively considered not necessary and is not recognised on the subjective side, — has in more recent times brought forth the thought that philosophy can begin only with a hypothetical and problematic truth, and that philosophizing can therefore at first be only a seeking; a view which Reinhold has repeatedly urged in the later period of his philosophizing, and to which justice must be done, that a genuine interest lies at its foundation, one which concerns the speculative nature of the philosophical beginning.

The examination of this view is at the same time an occasion to introduce a preliminary understanding of the meaning of logical progress in general; for that view already includes within itself the consideration of going forward.

It presents it in such a way that progress in philosophy is rather a going back and a grounding, through which alone it comes out that what one began with is not merely something arbitrarily assumed, but in truth partly the true and partly the first true.
zh: 这一洞见——绝对的真者必须是一个结果，反过来，一个结果又预设一个最初的真者，而后者因为是最初的，从客观方面看并不是必然的，从主观方面看也并不是被认识的——在近代催生了这样一种想法：哲学只能从一个假设的、问题的真理开始，因而哲学活动起初只能是一种寻求；这一观点是赖因霍尔德在其哲学活动的后期多次力主过的，而人们必须公正地承认：它的背后有一个真正的兴趣，那兴趣关涉哲学开端的思辨本性。
对这一观点的辨析同时也是一个契机，用来引出对逻辑推进之意义总体的初步理解；因为那一观点本身就已经包含了对「向前行进」的考量。
而且它是这样来设想的：哲学中的前进毋宁是一种回退与奠基，唯有通过这种回退与奠基才显出：人们据以开始的东西并非仅仅是任意假定的东西，而实际上是部分地是真者、部分地是最初的真者。

en: One must admit that it is an essential consideration — one which will emerge more closely within the logic itself — that going forward is a return into the ground, into the original and the true, upon which that whereby the beginning was made depends and is in truth brought forth.
— Thus consciousness is led back on its way from the immediacy with which it begins to absolute knowledge as its innermost truth.
This last, the ground, is accordingly that from which the first proceeds, which first appeared as the immediate.

— And still more, the absolute spirit, which emerges as the concrete and last highest truth of all being, is recognised as at the end of the development externalising itself with freedom and letting itself out into the shape of an immediate being, — resolving itself to the creation of a world which contains everything that fell into the development preceding that result, and which by this reversed position with its beginning is transformed into something dependent on the result as the principle.

What is essential for the science is not so much that a purely immediate is the beginning, but that the whole of it is a circuit within itself, in which the first is also the last and the last also becomes the first.
zh: 人们必须承认：有一项本质性的考察——它将在逻辑学内部更具体地显现出来——即：前进乃是一种向根据、向那原初而真实者的回归，而人们据以开始的那个东西依赖于它，并且实际上是由它产生出来的。
——这样，意识就在它从其所由开始的直接性出发的历程中，被引回到绝对知识——它最内在的真理。
这后者，即根据，也正是最初者由之而来的东西，而最初者首先是以直接者的身分出现的。
——更进一步，人们认识到：绝对精神——它作为一切存在的具体而最后的最高真理而显现出来——在发展的末尾以自由的方式外化自身、任自身逸出而成为直接存在的形态，——它决意去创造一个世界；这个世界包含着那先行于该结果的发展中所落入的一切，而那一切通过这一与自身开端的颠倒位置，转变为依赖于作为原则的结果的东西。
对科学来说，本质性的东西与其说是一个纯直接者作为开端，不如说是科学的整体本身就是一个自我内的循环，在其中最初者也就是最后者，而最后者也就成为最初者。

en: Hence on the other side it is equally necessary to consider that into which the movement returns as into its ground to be the result.

With this consideration in view the first is just as much the ground, and the last a derivative; in that one proceeds from the first and by correct inferences arrives at the last as at the ground, this [last] is the result.

Further, the progress from that which makes the beginning is to be regarded only as a further determination of the same, so that the beginning-and-end remains at the foundation of everything following and does not vanish from it.
Going forward does not consist in merely deriving another, or in passing over into a genuinely other; — and insofar as this passing over occurs, it cancels itself again just as much.
Thus the beginning of philosophy is the ground that is present in all the following developments and preserves itself, that which remains thoroughly immanent in its further determinations.
zh: 因此在另一方面，同样必要的是：把那个运动作为回归其根据而返回其中的东西看作结果。
由此看来，最初者同样就是根据，而最后者则是一个派生者；因为人们从最初者出发，通过正确的推论而抵达最后者、抵达根据，所以这最后者就是结果。
此外，从那个构成开端的东西出发的进展，只应当被看作它自身的一种进一步规定；这样一来，那开端即终结者便始终作为一切后继者的根据留存下来，而不会从中消失。
向前行进并不在于仅仅派生出另一个东西，也不在于过渡到一个真正别的东西；——而就这种过渡出现而言，它同样地又扬弃自身。
因此，哲学的开端就是那在一切后继发展中当下在场并且持存自身的根据，就是那始终内在地留存于其进一步规定之中的东西。

en: For through this progress the beginning loses what it has as something one-sided in this determinateness of being an immediate and an abstract in general; it becomes a mediated, and the line of scientific movement thereby makes itself into a circle.

— At the same time it emerges that that which makes the beginning, since it is therein the as yet undeveloped, the contentless, is not yet truly recognised in the beginning, and that it is only the science, and indeed the science in its whole development, which is its completed, contentful and only truly grounded cognition.
zh: 这样，通过这一进展，开端便失去了它在这一个规定性——即作为直接者并且作为一般意义上的抽象者——中所具有的单一性；它成为一个被中介者，而科学进展的这条线也就由此成为一个圆。
——同时也就显出：那个构成开端的东西，由于在开端中它还是未展开的、无内容的，因而在开端中还没有被真正地认识；而唯有科学——而且是处在其全部发展中的科学——才是对它的完成了的、充满内容的、并且第一次得到真正根据的认识。

en: But since the result only emerges as the absolute ground, the progress of this cognition is not something provisional, nor yet a problematic and hypothetical thing, but it must be determined by the nature of the matter and of the content itself.

That beginning is neither something arbitrary and merely provisionally assumed, nor one that appears arbitrary and is presupposed for convenience — of which, however, it becomes evident in the sequel that one did well to make it the beginning; it is not as with the constructions which one is obliged to make in order to prove a geometrical proposition, that it is only afterwards, from the proofs, that it emerges that one did well to draw exactly these lines and then to begin the proofs themselves with the comparison of these lines or angles; of itself, in this drawing of lines or this comparing, it is not comprehensible.
zh: 但是，由于结果只是作为绝对的根据才显现出来，这一认识的推进既不是什么临时性的东西，也还不是一个问题的、假设的东西；它必须由事情本身和内容本身的本性来决定。
那个开端既不是某种任性的、仅仅暂时被假定的东西，也不是那种显得任性、因而被姑且预设的东西——不过关于后者，人们日后终究会看出，把它作为开端乃是做对了的；这并不像那些为了证明一个几何命题而不得不作出的构造那样：在那种情形下，人们只是事后从证明中才看出，恰好画出这些线、并随后在证明本身中以这些线或角的比较为出发点乃是做对了的；就这种画线或比较本身而言，它是不可理解的。

en: Thus the ground why one begins in the pure science with pure being has already been indicated immediately in the science itself.
This pure being is the unity into which pure knowledge returns, or if this itself is still to be distinguished as a form of its unity, then it is also the content of that unity.
This is the aspect according to which this pure being, this absolutely immediate, is equally absolutely mediated.
But it must just as essentially be taken only in its one-sidedness of being the purely immediate, precisely because it is here the beginning.

Insofar as it were not this pure indeterminateness, insofar as it were determinate, it would be taken as something mediated, something already carried further; a determinate contains an other for a first.
It therefore lies in the nature of the beginning itself that it is being and nothing else.
It therefore needs no other preparations in order to enter philosophy, nor any further reflections and points of connection.
zh: 这样，为什么在这门纯粹的科学中要从纯粹的存在开始，其根据就已在科学自身之中被直接指出了。
这纯粹的存在就是纯粹知识所回归的那个统一；或者，如果连纯粹知识本身还应当被区别开来、作为它这一统一的形式而保持，那么这纯粹的存在也就是这一统一的内容。
这就是那个方面：按此而言，这纯粹的存在、这绝对直接者，同样是绝对被中介者。
但同样本质的是：它必须仅仅在它作为纯直接者的这一单一性上来把握，恰恰因为它在这里是开端。
就它不是这种纯粹的不确定性、就它被规定而言，人们就会把它当作被中介者、当作已经被进一步推进的东西；一个被规定者包含着对最初者而言的一个他者。
所以，开端本身的本性就在于：它是存在，此外别无任何。
因此，进入哲学并不需要别的准备，也不需要另外的反思和衔接点。

en: That the beginning is the beginning of philosophy — from this no more specific determination or positive content can really be taken for it.
For philosophy here, in the beginning, where the thing itself is not yet present, is an empty word or some adopted, unwarranted representation.
Pure knowledge gives only this negative determination: that it is to be the abstract beginning.
Insofar as pure being is taken as the content of pure knowledge, the latter must retire from its content, leave it to itself and determine it no further.

— Or if pure being is to be regarded as the unity into which knowledge at its highest point of reconciliation with the object has collapsed, then knowledge has vanished into this unity and left no difference from it and thus no determination for it.
— Otherwise too there is nothing present, no content of any kind, that could be used in order to make thereby a more determinate beginning.
zh: 从「开端是哲学的开端」这一点出发，实际上也无法为它取得任何更具体的规定或任何肯定的内容。
因为哲学在这里、在开端之处、在事情本身尚不存在的地方，还只是一个空词或某种被采纳的、没有根据的表象。
纯粹知识只给出这一个否定性的规定：它应当是抽象的开端。
就纯粹的存在被当作纯粹知识的内容而言，后者就必须从其内容退让，把内容留给它自己，不再对它作进一步的规定。
——或者，如果纯粹的存在应当被看作那个统一，即知识在其与客体达到最高和解的顶点上汇合进去的统一，那么知识就已经消失在这统一之中，没有留下与它的差别，因而也没有为它留下任何规定。
——此外也不存在什么东西或任何内容，可以被用来以此作出一个更具规定性的开端。

en: But even the determination of being assumed so far as the beginning could be left out, so that it would only be required to make a pure beginning.
Then there is nothing present but the beginning itself, and it would have to be seen what it is.

— This position could at the same time be made as a conciliatory proposal to those who, partly, are not satisfied with the fact that one begins with being, from whatever reflections it may be, and still less satisfied with the consequence that being has, of passing over into nothing, and partly simply do not know otherwise than that in a science one begins with the presupposition of a representation — a representation which is then analysed, so that the result of such analysis now gives the first determinate concept in the science.

If we observe this procedure too, we would have no particular object, because the beginning, as the beginning of thinking, is to be quite abstract, quite general, quite form without any content; we would thus have nothing at all but the representation of a mere beginning as such.
It is therefore only to be seen what we have in this representation.
zh: 但就连迄今为止被当作开端而假定的对存在的规定，也可以搁置不论；这样就只要求作出一个纯粹的开端。
那么所存在的就只有开端本身，而人们就得看看它是什么。
——同时也可以把这一立场作为一项善意的提议提给那些人：他们一部分并不满足于「从存在开始」（不管这出于何种反思），就更不满足于存在所带来的那个结果——过渡到无；另一部分则根本不知道别的，只知道在一门科学中总是以预设某个表象为开端——而这个表象随后将受到分析，以致这样一番分析的结果便给出这门科学中第一个有规定的概念。
如果我们连这一做法也观察一下，那么我们就没有任何特殊对象；因为开端作为思维的开端，应当是完全抽象的、完全普遍的、完全无形而无一切内容的形式；这样我们就只剩下「一个单纯的、作为这样的开端」的表象。
所以只需看看我们在这表象中拥有什么。

en: It is still nothing, and something is to become.
The beginning is not the pure nothing, but a nothing from which something is to proceed; being is therefore already contained in the beginning.
The beginning thus contains both, being and nothing; it is the unity of being and nothing, — or it is non-being which is at the same time being, and being which is at the same time non-being.
zh: 现在还是无，而它应当成为某物。
开端并不是纯粹的无，而是那种应当由之出发出某物的无；所以存在也早已包含在开端之中了。
所以开端同时包含两者：存在与无；它就是存在与无的统一——或者说，它就是那同时是存在的非存在，以及那同时是非存在的存在。

en: Further: being and nothing are present in the beginning as distinguished; for it points to something other; — it is a non-being which refers to being as to an other; the beginning-and-end is not yet there; it first belongs to being.
The beginning thus contains being, but as something which recedes from non-being or cancels it, as the opposite to it.
zh: 再者：存在与无在开端中是作为有差别者而存在的；因为开端指向某个别的东西；——它是一个非存在，它把存在当作一个他者而与之相关；那开端即终结者还不存在；它首先归属于存在。
所以，开端包含着存在，但却是作为一个远离非存在、扬弃了非存在、因而与它相对立的东西而包含着它。

en: Further, that which begins is already there; but just as much it is also not yet.
The opposites, being and non-being, are therefore in it in immediate union; or it is their undifferentiated unity.
zh: 再者，那开始的东西已经在了；但同样地，它也还不在。
所以对立者、存在与非存在，在它之中是直接统一的；或者说，它就是它们那无差别的统一。

en: The analysis of the beginning would thus give the concept of the unity of being and non-being — or, in a more reflected form, of the unity of being-differentiated and being-not-differentiated — or the identity of identity and non-identity.

This concept could be regarded as the first, the purest, i.e. the most abstract definition of the absolute, — as it would in truth be, if the question were at all about the form of definitions and about the name of the absolute.
In this sense, just as that abstract concept is the first, so all further determinations and developments would be only more determinate and richer definitions of this absolute.

But those who are not satisfied with being as the beginning, because it passes over into nothing and the unity of being and nothing arises from it, may consider whether they would be more satisfied with this beginning, which begins with the representation of the beginning, and with its analysis — which will indeed be correct, but likewise leads to the unity of being and nothing — than with making being the beginning.
zh: 对开端的分析于是给出存在与非存在的统一的概念——或者，以更反思的形式说，是差别状态与非差别状态的统一——或者是同一性与非同一性的同一性。
这一概念可以被看作绝对者的第一个、最纯粹的、即最抽象的定义——如果问题终究在于定义的形式和绝对者的名称，那么它事实上就会是这样的。
在这一意义下，正如那个抽象概念是第一个定义那样，一切进一步的规定与发展都只会是这同一个绝对者的更具规定性、更丰富的定义。
但是，那些因为存在过渡到无、由之产生出存在与无的统一，因而对「以存在为开端」不满的人不妨看看：对这个以「开端的表象」为开端、并以对这一表象的分析（这个分析大概会是正确的，但同样导向存在与无的统一）而来的开端，他们是否比对「把存在作为开端」更满意。

en: There is however a further consideration to be made about this procedure.
That analysis presupposes the representation of the beginning as known; it has been done in this way following the example of the other sciences.

These presuppose their object and assume for convenience that everyone has the same representation of it and may find in it roughly the same determinations which they bring and set forth from it by analysis, comparison and other reasoning.

But that which makes the absolute beginning must likewise be something known otherwise; if now it is a concrete, and so manifoldly determined in itself, then this relation which it is in itself is presupposed as something known; it is thereby given as something immediate, which it is not; for it is only a relation as a relation of distinguished ones, and so it contains mediation within itself.
Further, on the concrete there enters the contingency and the arbitrariness of the analysis and of determining in different ways.
Which determinations are brought out depends on what everyone finds in his immediate, contingent representation.

The relation contained in a concrete, in a synthetic unity, is a necessary one only insofar as it has not been found but has been brought forth through the movement of the moments themselves, through returning into this unity, — a movement which is the opposite of the analytical procedure, of an action external to the thing itself and falling into the subject.
zh: 不过关于这一做法还须作另一番考察。
那种分析预设了「开端的表象」为已知的东西；人们正是仿照其他科学的做法这样做的。
这些科学预设了它们的对象，并且姑且假定：人人对对象都有同样的表象，并且能在其中大致找到同样的规定——这些规定是它们通过分析、比较以及别的推理议论从对象那里东引西借地引来并给出的。
然而，那个构成绝对开端的东西，同样也必须是某种「另外已为人所知」的东西；但如果它是一个具体者、因而是自身内有多样规定的东西，那么它自身内的这种关系就被当作了某种已知的东西；这样它就被指明为某种直接的东西，而它其实并不是；因为它只是「作为有差别者之间的关系」的那种关系，因而在自身中包含着中介。
此外，在具体者上还出现了分析以及各种不同地加以规定的偶然性与任性。
会引出哪些规定，则取决于每个人在其直接而偶然的表象中所发现的东西。
一个包含在具体者、一个综合的统一之中的关系，只有在下述意义上才是必然的：它不是被找到的，而是通过诸环节自身的运动——通过返回这一统一——而产生出来的；——而这一运动恰恰是分析式做法的对立面，那种做法是一种外在于事情本身、落入主体之中的作为。

en: Herein is also contained the more precise point that that whereby the beginning is to be made cannot be a concrete, cannot be such a thing as contains a relation within itself.
For such a thing presupposes within itself a mediating and a passing over from a first to an other, of which the concrete that has become simple would be the result.
But the beginning is not itself to be already a first and an other; such a thing as contains a first and an other in itself already contains a going-away.
That which makes the beginning, the beginning itself, is therefore to be taken as a non-analysable, in its simple unfulfilled immediacy, thus as being, as the entirely empty.
zh: 这里还包含着更确切的一点：人们据以作出开端的东西，不能是一个具体者，不能是那种自身内含有某种关系的东西。
因为那样的东西预设了在其内部有一个从最初者到他者的中介与过渡，而那变得单纯的具体者就应当是这一过程的产物。
但开端本身不应当已经是最初者和他者；那样一个自身内含有最初者和他者的东西，已经包含了一种离去。
因此，那个构成开端的东西、开端本身，应当被看作一个不可分析者，一个处在其单纯而未被充实的直接性之中的东西，也就是被看作存在、被看作那全然空无的东西。

en: If anyone, impatient of the consideration of the abstract beginning, were to say that one should not begin with the beginning but quite directly with the thing itself, then this thing is nothing other than that empty being; for what the thing is, that is precisely what is first to emerge in the course of the science, and it cannot be presupposed as known before it.
zh: 如果有人不耐烦于对抽象开端的考察，想要说：不应当从开端开始，而应当径直从事物本身开始；那么这个事物不过就是那个空的存在而已；因为事物是什么，这正是应当在科学的历程中才首先显现出来的东西，它不能被预设为在这门科学之前就已为人所知的东西。

en: Whatever form be taken in order to have a beginning other than the empty being, it suffers from the deficiencies indicated above.
Those who remain dissatisfied with this beginning may call upon themselves to undertake the task of beginning in a different way, in order thereby to avoid these deficiencies.
zh: 无论采取何种形式以便获得一个不同于空的存在开端，它都受着上面所指出的那些缺陷之苦。
那些对这个开端仍不满意的人，不妨给自己提出这样的任务：用别的方式来开始，以便同时避开这些缺陷。

en: An original beginning of philosophy, however, cannot be left entirely unmentioned: the beginning with the I, which has made itself famous in more recent times.

It came partly from the reflection that everything following must be derived from the first truth, partly from the need that the first truth should be something known, and still more something immediately certain.
This beginning is not in general such a representation as is contingent and can be of one kind in one subject and of another kind in another.

For the I, this immediate self-consciousness, appears at first itself partly as an immediate, partly as something known in a much higher sense than any other representation; something else known does indeed belong to the I, but it is still a content distinguished from it and hence at once contingent; the I, on the contrary, is the simple certainty of itself.
But the I at all is also at the same time a concrete, or rather the I is the most concrete — the self-consciousness of itself as an infinitely manifold world.

For the I to be the beginning and ground of philosophy, the separation of this concrete is required, — the absolute act by which the I is cleansed of itself and enters its own consciousness as the abstract I.
Yet this pure I is now not an immediate, nor the known, the ordinary I of our consciousness, to which science should attach immediately and for everyone.
That act would in fact be nothing other than the elevation to the standpoint of pure knowledge, on which the difference between the subjective and the objective has disappeared.

But since this elevation is demanded so immediately, it is a subjective postulate; in order to prove itself as a true requirement, the movement of the concrete I from immediate consciousness to pure knowledge would have to have been exhibited and presented in it itself, through its own necessity.

Without this objective movement, pure knowledge, even when determined as intellectual intuition, appears as an arbitrary standpoint or even as one of the empirical states of consciousness, in respect of which it makes a difference whether one person finds it in himself or is able to bring it forth, and another person not.

But since this pure I must be the essential pure knowledge, and pure knowledge is posited only through the absolute act of self-elevation in the individual consciousness and is not immediately present in it, precisely the advantage is lost which was to accrue from this beginning of philosophy, namely that it is something known without qualification, which everyone finds immediately in himself and to which the further reflection can attach; that pure I is rather in its abstract essence something unknown to ordinary consciousness, something which it does not find in itself.

Thereby, on the contrary, the disadvantage of deception enters: that people are supposed to be speaking of something known, of the I of empirical self-consciousness, whereas in truth they are speaking of something remote from this consciousness.

The determination of pure knowledge as the I brings with it the continual recollection of the subjective I, whose limits are to be forgotten, and it keeps present the representation as if the propositions and relations which emerge from the I in the further development occurred in ordinary consciousness, since it is indeed that from which they are asserted, and could be found in it.
This confusion brings forth not immediate clarity but rather only a yet more glaring confusion and complete disorientation; outwardly it has occasioned the crudest misunderstandings.
zh: 不过，哲学中那个别出心裁的开端却不能不提及：那就是以「我」为开端，它在近来声名鹊起。
它一部分出自这样的反思：一切后继者都必须从最初的真者中派生出来；另一部分则出自这样的需要：最初的真者应当是一个已知的东西，而且更应当是一个直接的确定者。
一般说来，这个开端并不是那种偶然的表象，即在一个主体中可以是这回事、在另一个主体中又可以是另一回事的表象。
因为「我」、这一直接的自我意识，起初本身一部分表现为直接者，一部分表现为一个在远为更高的意义上比别的表象更为已知的东西；别的某种已知之物固然属于「我」，但它却还是一个与「我」有差别的、因而是立刻就偶然的内容；反之，「我」乃是它自身的单纯确定性。
但「我」总起来同时也是一个具体者；或者更确切地说，「我」乃是最具体者——是把自己意识为一个无限多样的世界的自我意识。
为了使「我」成为哲学的开端和根据，就必需把这个具体者分离出来——即那个绝对行为：「我」由此从自身中把自己清洗干净，并作为抽象的「我」进入自己的意识。
然而这纯粹的「我」现在并不是一个直接的东西，也不是那个已知的、我们意识中通常的「我」；科学本应直接地、对每一个人都从它上面接续起来。
那个行为其实无非是提升到纯粹知识的立场上；在这一立场上，主观与客观的差别消失了。
但由于这一提升被如此直接地要求，它就是一项主观的设定；要使它能作为真正的要求得到证明，就必须在它自身上、通过它自身的必然性，显示出并呈现具体「我」从直接意识向纯粹知识的运动。
没有这一客观的运动，纯粹知识即使被规定为智性直观，也显得只是一个任性的立场，甚至显得是意识的诸经验状态之一——就这一点而言，关键在于：某个人能在自身中找到它或能把它产生出来，另一个人却不能。
但既然这纯粹的「我」必须是本质的纯粹知识，而纯粹知识又只是通过个体意识中自我提升的那个绝对行为才被设定、并不是直接存在于其中，那么恰恰应当从这个哲学开端中产生的那个好处就失去了：即开端是一个全然已知的东西，每个人都能直接地在自身中找到它，并能在其上接续进一步的反思；那个纯粹的「我」毋宁在其抽象的本质性上，是某种为通常意识所不知道的东西，某种通常意识并不能在其中找到的东西。
这样一来，毋宁说倒是引入了幻觉的坏处：人们以为是在谈论某个已知的东西、即经验自我意识的「我」，而实际上谈论的却是某种远离这一意识的东西。
把纯粹知识规定为「我」，就随身带来对主观「我」的不停追忆——而这个「我」的界限本应被忘掉——并且使那种表象当下保持：仿佛在进一步发展中由「我」产生的那些命题与关系，在通常的意识中（因为通常的意识正是它们所被断言的那个「我」）会出现，并且能在其中被找到。
这种混淆与其说带来了直接的清晰，毋宁只带来了更加刺目的混乱和完全的迷失方向；在外部，它尤其挑起了最粗重的误解。

en: As for the subjective determinateness of the I in general, then pure knowledge will indeed take from the I its restricted significance, of having an insurmountable opposite in an object.
For this reason, however, it would at least be superfluous still to maintain this subjective attitude and the determination of pure essence as the I.
Yet this determination not only brings with it that disturbing ambiguity, but it also remains, on closer inspection, a subjective I.

The actual development of the science, which starts from the I, shows that the object has and retains in it the perennial determinateness of an other for the I, and thus that the I from which one starts is not the pure knowledge, which has in truth overcome the opposition of consciousness, but is still caught in appearance.
zh: 至于「我」总体的主观规定性，那么纯粹知识大概会剥夺「我」那种受限制的意义：即在一个客体上与它有着不可克服的对立。
但出于这个缘故，至少保留这种主观姿态以及把纯粹本质规定为「我」，便是多余的了。
然而这一规定不仅随身带来那种令人困扰的歧义，而且就近观察而言，它也仍然是一个主观的「我」。
科学的现实发展——它是从「我」出发的——表明：客体在其中保有并保持那种「对「我」而言是他者」的长存规定；因此，人们出发于其上的那个「我」并不是那已经在真理中克服了意识之对立的纯粹知识，而仍旧陷在现象之中。

en: Here it is still necessary to make the essential remark that, although in itself the I can indeed be determined as pure knowledge or as intellectual intuition and asserted as the beginning, what is at stake in science is not what is present in itself or inwardly, but the Dasein of the inner in thinking and the determinateness which such an inner has in this Dasein.

But what, in the intellectual intuition or — if its object is called the eternal, the divine, the absolute — what of the eternal or the absolute is present in the beginning of science, can be nothing other than the first, immediate, simple determination.

Whatever richer name is given to it than that which the mere being expresses, only this can come into consideration: how such an absolute enters into thinking knowledge and into the articulation of this knowledge.
The intellectual intuition is indeed a forcible rejection of mediation and of the demonstrative, external reflection.
What it does express beyond mere immediacy is something concrete: something containing in itself different determinations.

The articulation and the exposition of such a thing is, however, as has already been remarked, a mediating movement which begins from one of the determinations and proceeds to the other, even though this one goes back to the first; — it is a movement which at the same time must not be arbitrary or assertive.
What therefore is begun from in such an exposition is not the concrete itself, but only the simple immediate, from which the movement starts.
Moreover, if a concrete is made the beginning, there is lacking the proof which the connection of the determinations contained in the concrete requires.
zh: 在这里还必须作出那个本质性的说明：自在地说，「我」固然可以被规定为纯粹知识或智性直观，并被主张为开端；但在科学中所涉及的并不是自在地或内在地现成存在的东西，而是内在者在思维中的定在，以及这样一个内在者在这一定在中所具有的规定性。
然而，在科学开端中，在智性直观里——或者，若把它的对象称作永恒者、神圣者、绝对者——在永恒者或绝对者那里所存在的，就只能是第一的、直接的、单纯的规定。
无论给它一个比单纯存在所表达者更为丰富的名字，唯一需要考虑的只能是：这样的绝对者如何进入思维着的知识，并进入对这一知识的言说。
智性直观固然是对中介以及那种证明性的、外在的反思的强行拒斥。
而它所表达的多于单纯直接性的东西，是一个具体者：一个在自身中包含着相异的诸规定者。
然而，对这样一个东西的言说与陈述，正如已经指出的那样，是一种中介的运动：它从那些规定中的一个开始而走向另一个，尽管这另一个又返回到第一个；——这是一种同时又不容是任性的或断言式的运动。
因此，在这样的陈述中人们由之开始的，并不是具体者本身，而只是那单纯的直接者；这场运动是从它出发的。
而且，如果人们把一个具体者当作开端，那么那为具体者中所含诸规定的联结所需的证明就缺失了。

en: So, then, if in the expression of the absolute or the eternal or of God (and God would have the most undeniable right to have the beginning made with him), if there lies more in their intuition or thought than in pure being, then what lies hidden in them is to emerge first into knowledge as the thinking, not as the representing; whatever lies in them, be it as rich as it will, the determination which emerges first into knowledge is a something simple, for only in the simple is there nothing more than the pure beginning; only the immediate is simple, for only in the immediate is there as yet no going-away from one to another.

What thus is to be pronounced over being or contained in the richer forms of the representing of the absolute or of God, this is in the beginning only an empty word and only being; this lacuna, which otherwise has no further meaning, this emptiness is thus simply the beginning of philosophy.
zh: 那么，如果在绝对者、永恒者或上帝的表达中（而上帝有最不容争辩的权利，让人们从他开始），如果在他们的直观或思想中所含的比纯粹存在更多的东西，那么潜藏于其中的东西就应当首先作为思维、而不是作为表象进入知识；无论潜藏于其中的是什么，无论它多么丰富，首先进入知识的那个规定都是单纯者，因为只有在单纯者中才没有超出纯粹开端的东西；只有直接者才是单纯的，因为只有在直接者中才还没有从一个到另一个的离去。
因此，凡是要就存在而说出、或包含在对绝对者或上帝的表象的更丰富形式中的东西，在开端中只是空洞的字词，只是存在；这根别无他义的线索，这个空无，正是哲学的开端。

en: This insight is itself so simple that this beginning as such requires neither preparation nor any further introduction; and this preliminary character of reasoning about it could not have the intention of bringing it in, but rather of removing all preliminary character.
zh: 这一洞见本身是如此单纯，以至于这个开端作为这样的开端既不需要准备，也不需要进一步的导论；而这种关于它的推理议论的暂时性，其意图不可能是把它引进来，而毋宁是要消除一切暂时性。

en: Being is, firstly, determined against other in general; secondly, it is determining itself within itself; thirdly, since this provisional character of the division has been set aside, it is the abstract indeterminacy and immediacy in which it must be the beginning.
zh: 存在首先是对他者一般的规定；其次，它在自身之内规定自身；第三，当这种划分的暂时性被撇开时，它就是那抽象的不确定性与直接性，在其中它必须成为开端。

en: According to the first determination, being divides itself off against essence, in that in its further development it proves its totality to be only a sphere of the concept and sets against it another sphere as a moment.
zh: 按照第一个规定，存在分割自身而与本质相对立；因为在它进一步的发展中，它表明自己的总体性仅仅是概念的一个领域，并以另一个领域作为环节与它相对置。

en: According to the second, it is the sphere within which the determinations and the whole movement of its reflection fall.
Being will set itself therein in the three determinations:
zh: 按照第二个，它是那个领域：那些规定以及它自身反思的整个运动都落在这一领域之内。
存在将在其中把自己设定于这三个规定之中：

en: I. as determinateness as such; quality;
zh: I. 作为规定性本身；质；

en: II. as sublated determinateness; magnitude, quantity;
zh: II. 作为被扬弃的规定性；量，量；

en: III. as qualitatively determined quantity; measure.
zh: III. 作为质的规定的量；度。

en: This division is here, as has already been remarked in the introduction to these divisions in general, a provisional enumeration; its determinations have first to emerge from the movement of being itself, to define themselves thereby and to justify themselves.

About the divergence of this division from the usual presentation of the categories, namely as quantity, quality, relation and modality — which for Kant, incidentally, are only to be the titles for his categories, but are in fact themselves — only more general — categories — there is nothing to remark here, since the whole exposition will show what in general diverges from the usual order and significance of the categories.
zh: 这一划分在这里——正如在导论中就这些划分总体而言已经指出的那样——只是一种暂先的列举；它的诸规定首先必须从存在自身的运动中产生出来，由此得到自身的定义并得到自身的正当性。
关于这一划分与范畴通常排列方式之间的偏离——即把范畴排列为量、质、关系和模态，而这一点在康德那里原本不过是他的那些范畴的标题，实际上它们本身就是——不过更为一般的——范畴——在这里没有什么可说的，因为整个论述将会表明：究竟是什么在总体上偏离了范畴通常的秩序与意义。

en: Only this can perhaps be remarked, that otherwise the determination of quantity is set out before quality, and that this — like most things — without any further ground.
It has already been shown that the beginning makes itself with being as such, hence with qualitative being.
From the comparison of quality with quantity it is easy to see that the former is the first according to nature.

For quantity is quality which has already become negative; magnitude is the determinateness which is no longer one with being, but is already distinguished from it, the sublated quality which has become indifferent.

It includes the mutability of being, without the thing itself, being, whose determination it is, being changed through it; on the contrary, the qualitative determinateness is one with its being, does not go beyond it nor stand within it, but is its immediate limitation.
Quality is therefore, as the immediate determinateness, the first, and with it the beginning is to be made.
zh: 只有这一点或许值得提一下：通常量的规定是排在质之前的，而这一点——像大多数事情一样——并没有任何进一步的根据。
已经指出了：开端是与作为这样的存在相结合的，因而是与质的存在相结合的。
由质与量的比较可以轻易看出：质才是按本性而言的第一者。
因为量就是那已经成为否定性的质；而量是这样一种规定性：它不再与存在为一，而已经与存在相区别，它是那被扬弃的、变得无关紧要的质。
它包含着存在的可变易性，而那事情本身，即存在——它正是存在的规定——并不因它而改变；相反，质的规定性与其存在是一回事，它既不超出存在之外，也不处在存在之内，而是存在的直接受限性。
因此，质作为那直接的规定性，就是第一者；而开端应当与它一同造成。

en: Measure is a relation, but not the relation in general, but rather the relation determined of quality and quantity to one another; the categories which Kant comprehends under relation will take their place quite elsewhere.

Measure can also, if one wishes, be looked upon as a modality; but since with Kant these no longer constitute a determination of the content, but are only meant to concern the relation of the content to thinking, to the subjective, this is an altogether heterogeneous relation which does not belong here.
zh: 度是一种关系，但不是笼统的关系，而是质与量彼此相对规定的关系；康德归在关系之下的那些范畴，将在完全别的地方找到自己的位置。
度如果人们愿意，也可以被看作一种模态；但由于在康德那里模态不再构成内容的一个规定，而只涉及内容对思维、对主观者的关系，所以这是一种完全异质的、不属于这里的关系。

en: The third determination of being falls within the section of quality, in that it lowers itself as abstract immediacy to a single determinateness as against its others within its sphere.
zh: 存在的第三个规定落在质的这一节之内，因为存在作为抽象的直接性而把自己降低为与其自身领域内的其他规定相对的那一个单独的规定性。
